## Example 2.1 · (a–b) {#ss2-example-2-1-ab .sigma-example}

Evaluate the following expressions:

<div class="sigma-example-part"><span>a)</span><span data-math="\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{8}k^2">Sum from k = 1 to 8 of k squared</span></div>

<div class="sigma-example-part"><span>b)</span><span data-math="\displaystyle\sum_{k=3}^{7}(5k-1)">Sum from k = 3 to 7 of (5k − 1)</span></div>

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 6 · Example 2.1(a–b) · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
Preserve the booklet wording, bounds and expressions. Ask students to write the first and last substituted terms and count the terms before adding.

(a) 1+4+9+16+25+36+49+64=204. Eight terms.
(b) 14+19+24+29+34=120. Five terms, starting with k=3.

No arithmetic-series or sum-of-squares formula is required here. Calculator arithmetic can follow a correct expansion.
:::
